note: Public changelog for the website. Newest first. type: new | improved | fixed. Builds are TestFlight build numbers of version 1.0.0.

releases.title: Leave for Jumaat
releases.summary: A reminder to set off for Friday prayer, and the next prayer leads after sunrise.

changes.text: Leave for Jumaat lives with the prayer alarms. Choose how early, from 15 minutes to 2 hours, and in Singapore pick the first or second session.
Leave for Jumaat can ring as a real alarm, through silent mode and Focus, like the prayer alarms.
From Syuruk until Zohor, every look and widget now counts down to Zohor instead of showing Sunrise.

releases.title: Barakah Picks and a clearer masjid map
releases.summary: One small card of good causes near you, and a map that shows how far things are.

changes.text: Barakah Picks, one small card under Show more with good causes and halal businesses we check by hand for your country. You can turn it off in Settings.
The masjid map shows a beaming dot where you are, with rings at 1, 2 and 5 km.

releases.title: A quick guide, a Hijri calendar and a new Masjid tab
releases.summary: New users get a short tour, and the date on the Prayer screen opens a Hijri calendar.

changes.text: A short guide the first time you open the app, with a small phone that taps the real buttons. Replay it any time from Settings, Help.
Tap the date on the Prayer screen for the whole Hijri month, with the important days marked.
Free wall calendar and a whole Islamic year on one page, ready to print.
Rate and review, with a private note to us if something is wrong.
The Masjid tab shows the nearest five first, with walk or drive time, your own masjid, facilities and Friday prayer sessions in Singapore.

releases.title: Easier for everyone
releases.summary: Bigger text, screen readers and clearer colours across the app.

changes.text: Works with bigger text and with VoiceOver on iPhone and TalkBack on Android.
Deeper colours on the Colour Bands look, easier to read in daylight.
Ramadan last ten nights and the Tarawih counter in calmer colours.

releases.title: Opens straight away
releases.summary: No more waiting on Finding where you are.

changes.text: The app opens on your last place at once, then quietly checks where you are.

releases.title: Ramadan extras and a letter for work
releases.summary: More for Ramadan, and help asking for prayer breaks.

changes.text: Berbuka countdown widgets for the home screen.
A Tarawih counter for 8 or 20 rakaat.
A short letter that explains prayer breaks to your boss or your school, ready to print.
A note for long summer days in places far from the equator.
Times on the day the clocks change are right again.

releases.title: Ramadan in Malay and Indonesian
releases.summary: Ramadan screens in your language, and London times from the London Unified Prayer Timetable.

changes.text: Ramadan screens in Malay and Indonesian.
London now uses the London Unified Prayer Timetable.
Move my settings now carries your Ramadan fasts, Tarawih and juz.

releases.title: Widget fix
releases.summary: The big timetable widget shows the times again.

changes.text: The big timetable widget showed grey bars only. Fixed.

releases.title: Crash fix
releases.summary: The app opens again on every iPhone.

changes.text: Build 30 could close itself on opening. Fixed.

releases.title: Shorter prayer alerts
releases.summary: Alerts that are short and kind, in English, Malay and Indonesian.

changes.text: Prayer alerts use short lines that change each day.
Prayer names are in English by default. Change them in Settings.
A short moving clock greets you when the app opens. Turn it off in Settings.

releases.title: Same settings after a new phone
releases.summary: Delete the app or change phones and your settings come back.

changes.text: Your home, alarms and look come back after you delete the app or move to a new phone.
Your home place is only changed when you say so, with Change home.
Prayer alarms no longer ring again after Stop or Off.

releases.title: A short hadith where it helps
releases.summary: Short, authentic hadith in the right places, each with its reference.

changes.text: A short hadith beside the Prayer screen, tracker, alarms and Ramadan. Close any of them, or turn them off in Settings.
A new app icon, a compass ring with a fine kawung batik pattern, and the same look inside the app.

releases.title: Alarms for every prayer
releases.summary: Real alarms that ring, with Snooze.

changes.text: An alarm for any of the five prayers, with a choice of sound and Snooze for five minutes.
Big and Simple, large clear times with nothing extra on the screen.
One clear countdown, like 19m left to pray.
The Living Sky is easier to read by day.
Faster masjid search, with ready made lists for each country.

releases.title: Ready for Ramadan
releases.summary: Sahur to Raya, and alarms to wake up for Subuh.

changes.text: Ramadan and Syawal, with sahur and berbuka countdowns, fasting tracker and Raya.
Wake up for Subuh, a tahajjud alarm and a sahur alarm.
Quiet hours, buzz only alerts, a Jumaat reminder and your work calendar.
The Journey screen shows each prayer's plan when you travel.

releases.title: Worldwide, local authority first
releases.summary: Prayer times in 143 countries, following each country's religious authority.

changes.text: 143 countries, with the local religious authority first.
A reminder before each prayer, as well as the alert when it starts.
Prayer names in Arabic, Urdu, Bangla and French too.
Azan alerts and a pause in the prayer tracker for haid or illness.

releases.title: Our promises
releases.summary: Free forever, no outside ads, your data stays yours, open for anyone to see.

changes.text: The four promises are in the app, and the code is open for anyone to check.

releases.title: Print, find and move
releases.summary: A printable calendar, a better masjid search and an easy way to move your settings.

changes.text: Print a monthly prayer calendar for the fridge or the surau wall.
Move my settings to a new phone with a QR code, with nothing to sign up for.
Masjid search on iPhone uses Apple Maps and OpenStreetMap together, so more places show.

releases.title: Centre Dial first
releases.summary: The Prayer screen now opens on Centre Dial, and Classic list is renamed Side Dial.

changes.text: Centre Dial is the default Prayer screen until you pick another style with the palette button.
Classic list is now called Side Dial, to sit alongside Centre Dial.

releases.title: Day and night, everywhere
releases.summary: Automatic now follows the sky, a light/dark switch on the Prayer screen, a fifth style, and the big widget in every style.

changes.text: Centre Dial: the Day Dial in the middle, with the day and the list below.
Light/dark switch beside the style button: Automatic, Light or Dark.
Automatic follows the sky: bright from sunrise to Maghrib, a soft dim night after.
Every tab shares the same live sky (no more sun on Falak at night).
The big widget comes in every style: Classic list, Day Dial, Sun Path or Colour Bands, or the same as the app.

releases.title: Your look, one tap away
releases.summary: Switch Prayer screen styles from the Prayer screen, a simpler set of tabs, and travel features when you need them.

changes.text: Palette button on the Prayer screen: tap for the next style, touch and hold to pick one. Your choice is kept.
Settings is now a main tab: Prayer, Qibla, Falak, Masjid, Settings.
Musafir features are optional. When you land in another country we ask if you'd like jamak and qasar guidance; Journey opens from Settings or the plane chip.
Dhuha and the blessed night times are in English for everyone.
Masjid: an (i) button tells you who built the app, instead of a card at the end of the list.

releases.title: Four ways to see your day
releases.summary: Choose how the Prayer screen looks, and meet the people behind the app.

changes.text: Prayer screen styles in Settings > Display: Classic list (default), Day Dial, Sun Path and Colour Bands.
Day Dial: the whole day as a 24-hour ring in the colours of the sky, with every prayer time inside it.
Colour Bands: each prayer a full-width band of colour, a tribute to the classic Singapore timetable.
Sun Path: the sun's arc across today's sky, with each prayer marked on it.
Classic list fills the screen: everything, including Show more and the official MUIS source, without scrolling.
The Day Dial follows the natural colours of the day: bright dawn for Subuh, hot noon for Zohor, sunset for Maghrib, night for Isyak.
From the makers: Badal Haji & Umrah (Badal.sg) and NasarDigital, shown only under Show more and in Settings. Turn them off any time.

releases.title: One calm colour palette
releases.summary: The same colours everywhere, and a simpler Qibla compass.

changes.text: One colour palette across the whole app: brand peach, qibla gold, prayer colours only on prayer rows.
Qibla: the centre is a single arrow pointing at the qibla, instead of moving numbers.

releases.title: A new icon
releases.summary: A watch with the Ka'bah at its heart.

changes.text: New app icon: a compass-bezel watch with the Ka'bah at the centre and skeleton sword hands at 8:02.

releases.title: Times first
releases.summary: A redesign around what matters most: the prayer times.

changes.text: Large, clear times with AM/PM always on the same line; the countdown is small at the top.
Show more / Show less with Dhuha, the middle and the last third of the night (and Imsak in Ramadan). Free.
Light mode with a gently breathing sun and drifting clouds; Automatic, Light or Dark.
Falak is its own tab, with an AR camera view and a spirit level.
Prayer alerts at the exact time, with an optional early reminder and a Syuruk alert.
Qibla turns green when you face it, with a tick, a ripple and a tap, plus step-by-step instructions.
Prayer names follow you: Subuh or Fajr from your home country or phone, with the local word shown when you travel.
Big Home Screen widget: today's timetable, a mini version of the app.
New consistent icon set: prayer mat, compass, telescope, masjid and plane.

releases.title: Falak Mode
releases.summary: Find the qibla and Asr from the sun, the classical way.

changes.text: Falak Mode: Qibla Day, rashdul qiblat, shadow-stick Asr and sky signs, clearly labelled and pending review.
Ramadan and Eid dates with their sources, and 'My community follows' setting.
Subscribe to official prayer times in your calendar (MUIS and every JAKIM zone).
Help verify times where you are: send a masjid timetable photo, no account needed.
Travellers see today's combined (jamak) prayer windows.

releases.title: First build
releases.summary: Accurate, offline prayer times for Muslims living and travelling across Asia.

changes.text: Prayer times for every country in Asia, calculated on the phone and working offline.
Official timetables when online: MUIS (Singapore), JAKIM (Malaysia, by zone) and Kemenag (Indonesia).
Checked against a full year of official tables: offline times are never earlier than official.
Every day shows its source: official, masjid, community or calculated.
Travel mode: switches country method automatically, with musafir guidance and a trip log.
Qibla compass, nearby masjid and musollah search, Home and Lock Screen widgets, Live Activity countdown.
Optional prayer tracker with streak, and a Subuh wake-up alarm.
No third-party ads, no accounts, no tracking. Your location never leaves your phone.
